newsitem.title: INDIA: India awards rights to explore for oil and gas.
newsitem.headline: India awards rights to explore for oil and gas.

text.p: India has awarded a host of foreign and domestic companies rights to explore oil and gas in 14 blocks, a government spokesman said on Wednesday.
He said the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs had approved bids for 14 blocks, recommended by a official committee, in the seventh and eighth rounds in which 79 blocks were on offer.

Under the eighth round it approved bids for two blocks to U.S. Occidental International Exploration and Production Company and to a consortium of Reliance Industries Ltd and Enron Exploration Company, as well as to Assam Company Ltd and Medallion Company of the U.S., Larsen and Toubro and Tullow Oil Plc.
A consortium comprising Hindustan Oil Exploration Company and General Fibres (P) Ltd and another consortium between Essar Oil and HOEC were also among winners of contracts.
In the earlier six rounds the government had awarded contracts for 16 blocks and 19 fields.
In the seventh round two blocks have been offered to U.S. firms Rexwood Corporation and Oakland Oil Company which will operate jointly.
Opseis Inc has also been also awarded two contracts.
Others whose bids were approved for the round were domestic Essar Oil Ltd, Phoenix Overseas Ltd and Reliance Industries.
Joshi Technologies Inc was also one of the bidders.
The statement said under the seventh round 12 bids for 10 blocks, out of 45 blocks offered, were received. In the eighth round 33 bids for 18 blocks, out of 34 blocks, offered were received.
The CCEA also approved bids for exploration of 11 small fields.
The statement said after the awards the successful bidders would be required to execute a production-sharing contract with the government.
